paths.description: Public marketplace homepage and global navigation. Represents entry, search discovery, consent, preferences, and global chrome.
Torget search results for “sykkel”. Represents the primary search/listing journey, filters, result cards, and dense responsive UI.
Live marketplace item detail. Represents product metadata, gallery, seller/contact path, recommendations, and repeated gallery interaction.
Job landing page. Represents a second vertical and its primary navigation.
Editorial article with embedded marketplace items. Represents long-form content and article metadata.
Vend email login reached from FINN. Represents the authentication entry and input assistance.
Legacy marketplace search URL returning HTTP 404. Represents HTTP failure and recovery behavior.

findings.summary: The public experience does not adapt to dark color preference.
findings.evidence: The dark screenshot is byte-identical in composition to the default capture, and the home probe reports colorScheme “normal”, a white body background, and no prefers-color-scheme rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light/dark surface and text tokens, including the consent UI.

findings.summary: The cookie settings interstitial blocks the whole first viewport on every fresh visit.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show a full-page dimming layer and centered cookie dialog before the marketplace can be used. The DOM probe finds a full-viewport fixed #sp_message_container_1489005.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, content-preserving consent surface where legally possible. If modality is required, use a correctly named dialog with direct, equally available accept and reject actions and remembered state.

findings.summary: Consent choices are visually asymmetric.
findings.evidence: The consent screenshot gives “Godta alle” a solid black primary treatment while “Tilpass eller avvis” is outlined and requires another choice step.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer accept and reject at the same level with comparable prominence and plain language, without requiring an extra rejection journey.

findings.summary: State and route changes do not expose View Transition support.
findings.evidence: CSS probes across home, search, detail, job, and article report no view-transition declarations or opt-in metadata.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance route and high-value state changes with same-document or cross-document View Transitions, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Global chrome does not respond to scroll state.
findings.evidence: The probes find no scroll-state query, scroll timeline, or scroll-driven declarations on the inspected homepage, listing, and detail templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a sticky header with scroll-state container queries or a lightweight progress/affordance treatment where long pages need orientation.

findings.summary: Most reusable marketplace templates do not use component-level queries.
findings.evidence: Only the article probe reports any @container rule. Home, search, detail, and job probes report none despite cards and filters being reused at different widths.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable cards, filter groups, and search controls containment and adapt them with size container queries, retaining viewport fallbacks where needed.

findings.summary: The HTTP 404 state is a dead end.
findings.evidence: The tested legacy search URL returns HTTP 404 and renders title “Usjda”, H1 “404”, no links, no landmarks, and no recovery action.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a useful 404 with search, home and relevant category links, preserve the attempted query when possible, and announce the error clearly.

findings.summary: Load performance and stability miss Core Web Vitals expectations.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports homepage LCP 10.0 s and detail LCP 37.1 s. Mobile layout captures report CLS 0.138 on search and 0.116 on detail; search also records a 214 ms long task.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile LCP discovery and dependency chains, reserve late UI space, and split or defer noncritical JavaScript and consent/advertising work.

findings.summary: Images do not consistently reserve dimensions.
findings.evidence: The image primitive reports missing width and height on all 15 homepage images and all 11 detail images. Layout evidence records CLS above 0.11 on home/detail and 0.138 on search.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio on every image and preserve the slot through responsive source changes and lazy loading.

findings.summary: Critical resource delivery is excessively heavy and redirect-rich.
findings.evidence: The homepage HAR records 174 requests and 5.32 MB transferred, including 86 scripts totaling 4.51 MB, 37 redirects, repeated parser-blocking stylesheets, and several uncached CMP assets.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove version-alias redirects, consolidate critical CSS, compress text, cache immutable assets, preload only true LCP dependencies, and defer noncritical podlets.

findings.summary: Duplicate framework and design-system payloads dominate the load.
findings.evidence: HAR offenders include two ~456 KB Warp Elements bundles, Warp React 18 and React 19 payloads, plus multiple React versions. JavaScript is 4.51 MB transferred before the core homepage is usable.
findings.suggestedFix: Align podlets on one runtime and Warp version, share singleton dependencies, conditionally load below-fold and advertising code, and use coverage to remove unused modules.

findings.summary: Important controls and recommendation images lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse finds the homepage search role=dialog unnamed and its combobox missing aria-expanded. On detail it finds an unnamed finance slider and multiple recommendation images without alt.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native semantics where possible; otherwise provide complete names, required ARIA state, and meaningful or empty alt text according to image purpose.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not consistently visible.
findings.evidence: The article focus probe focuses the “Motor” navigation link and reports a transparent 2 px outline with no box shadow. Other templates show a visible cyan outline, so the behavior is inconsistent.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply a shared :focus-visible treatment with sufficient contrast across all navigation and interactive components, including article chrome.

findings.summary: The detail page emits a console error during load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse records console.error from sourcepoint/anonymous.js: “No Pulse integration detected. Aborting.”
findings.suggestedFix: Make optional analytics integration detection non-erroring and remove production console noise while preserving actionable diagnostics.

findings.summary: The editorial article lacks article-specific structured metadata.
findings.evidence: The article probe finds a descriptive title and Open Graph fields but only Organization JSON-LD, not Article/NewsArticle metadata for the visible long-form content.
findings.suggestedFix: Add Article JSON-LD that matches the visible headline, image, publication date, author/publisher, and canonical URL, and include og:url.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced security policy and cookie hygiene are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence reports no Content-Security-Policy and no Permissions-Policy. Cookie evidence reports _gcl_au and __mbl without Secure and _sp_su with SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP, a least-privilege Permissions-Policy, and Secure cookies with the narrowest workable SameSite policy.

findings.summary: Tracking requests begin while the consent interstitial is still unresolved.
findings.evidence: The same fresh-load session displays the cookie dialog while the tracker primitive records DoubleClick and Google Tag Manager among 13 third-party origins; the HAR attributes 5.25 MB and 167 requests to non-main origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate nonessential advertising and analytics until valid consent, minimize vendors and events, and batch the remaining measurement.

findings.summary: Homepage and detail core content do not present a usable first viewport without JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Discoverability crawler screenshots for home and detail are blank in the captured viewport. Raw/rendered word coverage is 44% on home and 68% on detail, while search is 89% and visibly server rendered.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the primary heading, search entry, item title, price and core action above the fold, then hydrate enhancements without hiding the base markup.

findings.summary: Homepage image delivery wastes bytes and eager work.
findings.evidence: The image primitive reports 13 oversized images, 13 below-fold images without lazy loading, 13 without srcset, and 8 legacy-format images.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit responsive srcset/sizes, modern formats where beneficial, lazy-load below-fold cards, and select image dimensions close to rendered size.

findings.summary: Inspected CSS is not prepared for alternate writing directions.
findings.evidence: The search template declares lang=nb, but the accessible authored CSS probe counts 238 physical left/right declarations and no logical inline/block declarations.
findings.suggestedFix: Prefer logical margin, padding, inset, and sizing properties in shared components so future localization and bidirectional content do not require forks.

taskList.title: Cut and deduplicate critical JavaScript/CSS and repair LCP/CLS
Gate trackers and harden CSP, policies, and cookies
Make consent non-obstructive and choices equally prominent
Repair accessible names, ARIA state, alt text, and article focus
Server-render usable first-viewport content on home and detail
Add useful recovery to HTTP failure pages
Add dark preference support and modern responsive/transition enhancements
Add Article structured data and remove production console noise
